current_date: 12 September 2022 (council page link text 'Checklist 004 - To be used from 12 September 2022'; news article of 20 Sep 2022). The document itself is undated but mentions BNG for minor applications from 2 April 2024, so it was revised in or after early 2024.
current_evidence: The Havering planning application process page links this same file ID (5748) as 'Checklist 004 - To be used from 12 September 2022'. A council news article of 20 September 2022 confirms the new lists took effect on 12 September 2022. No newer list or consultation was found; the only consultation (Nov 2021 to Jan 2022) led to this list.

issues.detail: The List date of 2024-03-01 comes from PDF metadata. The council's own text dates the list from 12 September 2022, when it took effect. The PDF is undated and only shows it was revised after early 2024, through its BNG-for-minors reference. The workbook should give the 12 Sept 2022 effective date and note the 2024 revision.
issues.evidence: Council page link text: 'Checklist 004 - To be used from 12 September 2022'; news article 20 Sep 2022: updated validation lists took effect 12 September 2022

issues.detail: The Validation list URL points only to Checklist 004, which covers 'All applications except Householder Applications'. The householder list is a separate file, Checklist 001 (file 5747). Other type-specific checklists linked from the same page were not read. They include 011 (listed building), 012 (adverts), 014/015 (lawful development certificates), 016-022 (agricultural, demolition and telecoms prior notifications) and 031 (tree works).
issues.evidence: Checklist 004 heading: 'All applications except Householder Applications'
issues.grok_comment: The List_URL does point only to Checklist 004, but the LBC, advert, LDC, prior-notification and tree-works checklists are all present in raw/london_borough_of_havering/, so they were fetched; their content just wasn't mapped (several say "There are no local planning application requirements").
issues.claude_response: Partly accepted. The other checklists were fetched but not mapped.

issues.detail: The Outline and Reserved matters rows come from older Checklists 005 and 023. These cite DMPO 2010, the EIA Regs 2011, GDPO 1995 and the 'LDF Proposals Map', so they pre-date the 2021 Local Plan and the September 2022 Checklist 004, which states it covers all non-householder applications including outline. As a result, old triggers appear in the workbook. One example is the Parking row's '200 spaces', which is actually the old Air Quality trigger.
issues.evidence: Checklist 005 references 'Development Management Procedure Order 2010', 'EIA Regulations 2011', 'LDF Proposals Map'

issues.detail: The Householder Flood Risk Assessment trigger is the structural survey sentence ('The assessment can form part of the Flood Risk Assessment or Structural Survey reports') plus the Regulation 4 boilerplate. Checklist 001 actually requires an FRA for all development in Flood Zones 2 and 3.
issues.evidence: Checklist 001 FRA: 'All development in Flood Zones 2 and 3 (including those benefitting from defences)'

issues.detail: The Householder CIL form trigger is a biodiversity sentence ('Where the proposal may have an impact on wildlife and biodiversity...'). The real trigger is householder applications that create 100 sqm or more of new floorspace (GIA).
issues.evidence: Checklist 001 CIL: householder applications proposing new floorspace of 100 sqm or more (GIA)

issues.detail: Several Householder triggers are content descriptions or boilerplate, not triggers. Structural Survey and Arboricultural give only the Regulation 4 NOTE. The real triggers are a basement, or substantial demolition or structural work to a listed or conservation-area building, and trees or hedges on or adjacent to the site. Basement Impact Assessment gives 'level of information ... commensurate' instead of 'new or extended basement'. Heritage and Ecological list what the report must include. Energy/Sustainability omits that a householder needs a Sustainable Design and Construction Statement only for 'extensive retrofit works'.
issues.evidence: Checklist 001 Structural Survey: 'Required for all applications where a basement is proposed'; Sustainability: 'proposing extensive retrofit works to improve the environmental performance of the building'

issues.detail: Checklist 001 has no householder item called 'Highways / access details (visibility splays)'. The excerpt 'site including access arrangements.' is a fragment of the site plan guidance.

Several rows duplicate others with the same excerpt. 'Street scene elevations / Contextual drawings' repeats 'Photographs / Photomontages' (Householder and Full). 'Sunlight to gardens/amenity space' repeats 'Daylight / Sunlight' (Householder and Full). 'Marketing / vacancy evidence' repeats 'Employment / Economic Statement'. 'Housing mix / dwelling standards' is part of the Accessibility Statement content.
issues.evidence: Identical excerpts, e.g. 'Consent CGI/Photomontages, Photographs & Contextual Drawings May be required...'

issues.detail: The Full planning 'Sequential / Exception Test (flood)' row uses the town-centre sequential test text: edge or out-of-centre uses of 200 sqm or more. This is a retail sequential test mislabelled as a flood test, and it duplicates the Retail/Town Centre row. Checklist 004's flood items are the FRA and the flood defence details.
issues.evidence: Excerpt: 'Assessment and Sequential Test Required for all applications for new, or extensions to existing, edge or out-of-centre uses ... 200 sq m or more'

issues.detail: Many Full planning triggers are garbled or belong to a neighbouring item. Planning Statement shows the heads-of-terms text; the real trigger is all major development, including change of use over 1,000 sqm. Viability merges into the ventilation text. Waste Management Plan merges into the viability text; it applies to all major development. Drainage/SuDS shows only 'is provided in the relevant section below'; the real trigger is all major development. Crime prevention reads 'All strategicError!'; the source item is the Safer Places Statement, all major development. Open space merges into the noise guidance references. The floor plans trigger is the listed-building 1:20 and photomontage text. Ventilation lists content; the real trigger is food preparation or substantial ventilation equipment. Heritage lists content; the real trigger is the curtilage of a listed building, park or scheduled monument, conservation areas or APAs, or major development within 50m of a conservation area.
issues.evidence: Crime prevention excerpt ends 'Structural Survey All strategicError!'

issues.detail: The BNG trigger reads 'Required for all Major applications', but Checklist 004 also requires BNG for all minor applications from 2 April 2024.
issues.evidence: Checklist 004 BNG: all major applications; all minor applications from 2 April 2024

issues.detail: The Full planning 'Pre-application advice / engagement details' row ('Pre-application discussions should be held with the Waste & Recycling Team' plus Local Plan adoption boilerplate) is advice, not a validation requirement. Many tab_items are also process text or fragments. They include the repeated 'Regulation 4 of the Town and Country Planning (Applications) Regulations 1988' NOTE, hard-copy instructions, Planning Portal file-size limits (25Mb/5Mb) and broken URL fragments such as 'tination/Dust%20and%20Emissions...' and 'nated_land_inspection_strategy.pdf'.

Many Checklist 004 requirements were not captured as requirement rows. Affordable Workspace Statement: industrial sites and major commercial or mixed-use schemes. Circular Economy Statement: strategic applications. Construction Logistics Plan: all major. Employment and Skills Plan: all major. Flood defence details: development adjacent to the tideway. Food and Beverage Management Plan: restaurants, pubs and micro breweries. Foul Sewerage and Utilities Assessment: major development connecting to or altering utilities. Landscaping Strategy: all major except change of use; it appears only under Minerals & waste. Parking Design and Management Plan: new development providing parking. Servicing and Delivery Plan: strategic or non-residential development generating servicing. Statement of Community Involvement: all major. Structural Survey: basements, retained structures, listed or conservation-area structural works. Sustainable Design and Construction Statement: all major. Transport Assessment/Statement: DfT Appendix B thresholds. Urban Greening Factor: all major except B2/B8. 3D massing model (.FBX): all major. Landfill Statement: depositing waste. Detailed drawings: listed building works. The SCI, landfill and 3D model appear only as tab_item fragments.
issues.evidence: Checklist 004 local requirements list, e.g. 'Affordable Workspace Statement: Required for industrial sites, major commercial and mixed-use applications'

issues.detail: Two Checklist 001 items are missing from the Householder rows. Noise (and vibration) Impact Assessment: applications raising disturbance issues for neighbours, or in noise-sensitive locations. Detailed Drawings: works to a listed building.
issues.evidence: Checklist 001 items 9 'Detailed Drawings - Listed Building' and 18 'Noise (and vibration) Impact Assessment'

issues.detail: Listed building consent and Advertisement consent are marked '(none)'. Havering publishes dedicated checklists for both (011 and 012), which Grokbot did not read. Checklists 001 and 004 also require detailed drawings for listed building works and a heritage statement where a listed building is affected.
issues.evidence: Council page lists 'Checklist 011' and 'Checklist 012' under listed building and advertisement consent
issues.grok_comment: Correct that LBC and Advertisement are '(none)' although their checklists list local items (LBC: "Heritage Statement Always Required"; adverts: "Lighting Assessment All illuminated hoardings"); but both checklists were downloaded (raw/london_borough_of_havering/e8b0c0c116 and ccc03a7dee), so it is a capture failure rather than not read.
issues.claude_response: Partly accepted. The checklists were downloaded but not mapped, so the (none) rows are still wrong. Reworded as a mapping failure.

issues.detail: Some rows are placed under the wrong application types. Design Code is under Full planning, but the source requires it for outline or hybrid major applications where scale or layout is reserved. Telecommunications supplementary information is under Full planning, but it applies to mast and antenna development by operators, normally telecoms prior approval (Checklist 020). The Landscaping scheme appears only under 'Minerals & waste (county)', triggered by a 'waste (landfill)' fragment, but the source applies it to all major development. 'Schedule of works (listed building)' is under Householder and Full planning with no listed-building qualifier.
issues.evidence: Checklist 004 Design Code: outline or hybrid major applications where scale and/or layout are reserved

issues.detail: Outline rows have triggers taken from the wrong item. Flood Risk Assessment shows the town-centre-uses text. Landscaping and Lighting both show the contaminated-land text. Ventilation/Extraction shows the tree survey text. The Daylight, Energy and EIA rows under Outline quote the reserved-matters checklist (023: 'For approval of reserved matters in relation to Layout and/or Scale').
issues.evidence: Outline Ventilation excerpt: 'Where there are trees or hedges on the proposed development site...'

summary: Grokbot links Havering's current list (Checklist 004, in use from 12 Sept 2022, revised for BNG in 2024). The 2024-03 date is metadata only, and the link covers non-householder applications only. The extraction contains many triggers taken from adjacent items (householder FRA and CIL, a flood sequential test that is really a retail test) and duplicate rows, and uses outdated outline/RM checklists. It misses about 18 Checklist 004 items, including affordable workspace, construction logistics, UGF, SCI and the sustainable design statement.
